chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majilawayh narrated to us, he said: My uncle Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim narrated to me, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi, from his father, from Khalaf ibn Hammad al-Asadi, from Abu al-Hasan al-Abdi, from al-A'mash, from Ubayyah ibn Rabee, from Abdullah ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his Family) said:

Whoever wishes to hold fast to the solid rope which has no breakage, let him hold fast to the Wilayah (Divine Authority) of my brother and my Successor, Ali ibn Abi Talib. Indeed, he who loves him and befriends him will not perish, and he who hates him and antagonizes him will not be saved.

key_terms.الْعُرْوَةُ الْوُثْقَى: The Solid Rope (Quranic term for firmest hold)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of Ali ibn Abi Talib as the 'Solid Rope' in Shia theology?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Mani al-Akhbar* explicitly identifies Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib as the 'solid rope' (al-'Urwah al-Wuthqa) of Quran 31:22, grounding the Shia doctrine of Wilayah in divine textual evidence. It establishes a theological causality where attachment to Ali ensures salvation and enmity toward him leads to perdition, a concept central to Shia exegesis regarding the necessity of recognizing the Imams for the validity of faith.
